instructions:
Return JSON only, no markdown, with exactly {"listening":{"title":"...","focus":"...","part":"Part 1|Part 3|Part 4","script":"...","questions":[{"title":"...","prompt":"...","options":["...","...","...","..."],"answer":0,"explanation":"..."}]},"reading":{"title":"...","focus":"...","passage":"...","questions":[{"title":"...","prompt":"...","options":["...","...","...","..."],"answer":0,"explanation":"..."}]}. Generate exactly five Listening and five Reading questions. The Listening script is for synthetic browser voice, not official audio; make one original conversation or monologue of about 300–400 words and five questions that follow information order. Include paraphrase and one change/correction or qualification. Set part to Part 1 for an everyday social needs/services conversation, Part 3 for an academic discussion, or Part 4 for a single-speaker academic monologue; make transcript format agree with this choice. The Reading passage is original and self-contained, about 400–500 words; questions follow passage order, with at least one carefully limited inference and one distinguishing author claim from an example. Each question must be answerable solely from its script/passage and have exactly one defensible correct option. Use four concise plausible non-overlapping options, distribute answer indexes across 0–3, and explain the evidence plus why the strongest distractor fails. Keep each option under 12 words and each explanation to 1–2 sentences; do not repeat source paragraphs in explanations. Avoid trick questions, external knowledge, ambiguous quantifiers, and unsupported inference. Keep all content original; do not reproduce, paraphrase closely, or claim to use official IELTS questions. Do not provide a model essay, sample response, answer band, IELTS score, or score conversion. Write natural international English and keep names, figures and dates internally consistent. Stage IELTS 5.0 to 6.0: paraphrase, linked ideas, corrected details, and clear comparisons across familiar academic topics. Ensure the language demand and reasoning complexity fit this learning stage while remaining original practice, not a validated band test. Suggested original topic space: a public clinic appointment reminder trial, a college careers-fair feedback summary, and a city park accessibility audit. Do not use Linear Thinking as a level/category label: pathwayStage is the stage classification; method guidance is separate.
Repair the supplied Listening and Reading batch against the findings. Return the complete objective JSON shape, preserving every valid unflagged passage, script, question, answer key and explanation. Keep exactly five Listening and five Reading questions, four distinct options per choice question, and one clearly supported correct answer. The Listening script must contain 300–400 whitespace-separated words, retain its current appropriate IELTS part and remain consistent with its questions. Do not add model answers, band estimates or official claims.

currentBatch.reason: Script is a two-way everyday transactional conversation about clinic appointment details, time correction, and reminder arrangements - classic Part 1 social needs/services, not an academic student/staff discussion (Part 3) or single-speaker academic monologue (Part 4).

findings.issue: Stem asks what David MUST do to confirm, but keyed Reply YES is optional: script explicitly permits confirmation during the phone call instead. Ask How can David confirm? or provide the complete alternative Reply YES or confirm during the phone call; retain unique supported key/explanation.
